masque

Synthetic copies of confidential data tables, for writing analysis code without the real data.

masque makes a synthetic copy of a confidential table. Analysts write and test code on the copy without seeing the real values. The data owner then runs the finished code on the real data, using a private recipe that maps the codes in the copy back to the real labels.

By default, every outcome and covariate is simulated independently, with no link to other columns or to the real rows. Each numeric column keeps only an eleven-point summary: its 1st percentile, deciles and 99th percentile. The experimental design and the pattern of missing values are kept exactly, and category labels are replaced by codes. When the code needs correlations between columns, use mode = "collaborate", or mode = "local" if the copy will not leave the data owner. Treatment effects can also be mimicked by setting conditional = TRUE. Each step discloses more about the real data, and masque gives no formal privacy guarantee.

It is for owners of confidential research data who want an outside analyst to build the analysis without seeing the real values, and for the analysts who build it. The input can be a single table, a folder of files or a multi-sheet workbook.

The changelog lists what changed in each release.

Every table masque returns is a data.table.

Installation

Pre-built binaries from r-universe:

install.packages(
  "masque",
  repos = c("https://max578.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org")
)

Or from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("max578/masque")

Two-minute example 

library(masque)

# Read a small public fixture (alpha-design field trial; John & Williams, 1995).
f  <- system.file("extdata", "john_alpha.csv", package = "masque")
df <- read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = TRUE)

# One guided call: read -> propose roles -> (review) -> mask -> audit.
# In an interactive session it pauses to let you review the plan;
# ask = FALSE skips the pause. The default copy keeps the design and the
# missing values; every other value is drawn independently.
m <- masque(df, seed = 1L)

synth <- synthetic(m)   # hand this to the analyst
rec   <- recipe(m)      # keep this private

# Analyst builds a pipeline against the synthetic namespace ...
fit <- lm(yield ~ gen + rep, data = synth)

# ... and the data owner re-targets it to the original data.
preds <- predict(fit, newdata = apply_recipe(df, rec))

# A description of the clone the analyst can plan with: sizes, roles and
# counts, never a value.
card <- data_card(m, name = "alpha_trial")

A folder of files or a multi-sheet workbook works the same way. Pass the path to masque() and it masks every table at once, aliasing shared keys consistently so the synthetic tables still join.

If the table needs tidying first, clean_table() makes column names valid and trims whitespace, and conform_table() merges near-duplicate labels and sets column types, reporting each change.

Multi-environment trials

detect_design() recognises environment columns, such as site or year, and the design within each environment. By default, and in collaborate mode, the environment labels are replaced by codes and every row stays in its environment. The clone does not keep genotype-by-environment effects, so it is no substitute for the real data in scientific inference.

Known-truth controls

A pipeline developed on the clone can be checked against datasets in which the answer is known. A control spec, declared once, names the column to reassign, the design strata it is permuted within, the outcome an effect is planted on and the size of that effect. From it, controls() derives a null (every analysed column permuted), negative replicates (one column permuted within strata) and positive replicates (the negative plus the planted shift), by permutation alone. The same spec runs on the clone for the analyst and, with a private seed, on the original for the owner, who returns a verdict about the pipeline rather than a dataset.

spec <- control_spec(on = "gen", target = "yield", effect = list(sd = 0.5),
                     strata = "rep", n = 19L, seed = 2026L)
ctl <- controls(synthetic(m), roles(m), spec)
control_table(ctl, "positive", 1L)

A masque_plan() holds the roles and the spec together, so the spec is fixed before any real result exists. mask(df, plan) resolves it on the source, handover() gives the analyst the clone and the plan in clone vocabulary, and controls(real, plan, recipe = rec) runs it on the owner’s side.

Threat model

masque gives no formal privacy guarantee such as differential privacy. It makes copies for writing analysis code, with explicit confidentiality safeguards. Read Confidentiality and the threat model before using it.

What masque does

  • Preserves enough structure for pipelines to run unchanged.
  • Provides three modes.
    • null, the default, keeps the design and the missing values exactly. It draws each numeric value from its column’s 1st percentile, deciles and 99th percentile, and each categorical value uniformly over the column’s levels, which are renamed to codes.
    • local keeps the real structure (correlations, and real labels unless you code them). It keeps identifiers and free text and runs no audit, so its output is for the data owner only.
    • collaborate keeps the correlations, replaces treatment and category labels with codes (numeric treatment levels included), adds small random noise within each value’s measurement resolution, and runs the leakage audit.
  • In the null and collaborate modes, columns that look like identifiers or free text are dropped. They are found by name (such as id, email or farmer) or by mostly distinct character values, so a numeric identifier with an ordinary name can pass: review the proposed roles. A column that would be resampled from a table of fewer than five rows is refused.
  • The leakage audit compares the copy with the original, column by column and for the table as a whole. A HIGH finding raises a warning and blocks masque’s own writers until it is resolved or overridden.
  • Synthesises a column that is constant within a trial or site once per unit, so the clone keeps one value per trial, and keeps linked event times in order (events =).
  • Keeps treatment, block and environment means on request (conditional = TRUE, in local or collaborate mode). Treatment means on the clone then track those of the real data, and block and environment effects stay detectable. What a conditional clone keeps of the design tests this on eight field designs.
  • Records every translation (column names, factor levels) in a private recipe. The recipe holds the real labels, the original column names and the seed, so together with the synthetic it undoes every alias. Keep it with the original data and never send it with the synthetic.
  • Audits its own output (audit_mask()), raises HIGH findings as classed warnings the guided flow never silences, and refuses package-managed writes while a HIGH finding stands (an explicit allow_high = TRUE override is available, warned and recorded in the recipe).

What masque does not do

  • It is not a universal anonymiser, and it does not provide differential-privacy guarantees.
  • It does not make outputs safe for public release.
  • It does not anonymise rare strata, small designs, or operational metadata (small site-by-year combinations, contact names, geolocations).
  • It does not certify compliance with any privacy, health, banking, or research-governance obligation. It can contribute evidence to such a decision; the decision itself is organisational and legal.
  • It does not rewrite arbitrary pipeline source code.

Bottom line. Generating a synthetic table is not a release decision. In the Five Safes framework for controlled data access, masque contributes to Safe Data and Safe Outputs; Safe People, Safe Projects, and Safe Settings are governance questions no package can answer. The collaborate workflow assumes only the synthetic crosses the trust boundary.

Related packages

  • synthpop makes synthetic versions of confidential microdata for release, synthesising one variable at a time from conditional models, and measures their utility and disclosure risk.
  • sdcMicro anonymises microdata for public- and scientific-use files and estimates disclosure risk.

Both produce data meant to be analysed in place of the original. masque produces a development copy: analysts write code on it and the data owner runs that code on the real data through the private recipe. It keeps the experimental design (treatments, blocks, plots), and a conditional clone (conditional = TRUE) also keeps the treatment means of the outcome. Every column’s role and action is checked against a fixed vocabulary before anything is masked.
